Skip to content
Журнал
/
The White Tower Yekaterinburg’s Constructivist symbol becomes Russia’s cultural heritage site
Сообщить о проблеме
The designers of a water tower whose construction began in 1929 in a settlement near Uralmash machinery plant could hardly imagine that this structure would become known by its proper name, turn into a city landmark and acquire the status of an architectural monument, only to be abandoned for more than half a century.
In 1920s in Sverdlovsk, as Yekaterinburg was called at that time, construction of Uralmash started. The plant was to become the flagship of Soviet heavy machinery industry. Industrial township grew around it, and the problem of water supplies arose. It was decided to pump water from the nearest lake, Shuvakish.
A creative approach was taken, and the contest for the design of the water tower was announced. The winner was a young architect Moisei Reischer who was 26 at that time. He came up with a unique design overnight. After some minor tweaks and addition of round windows, the project was accepted for execution.
Uralmash construction workers began to erect the tower under the guidance and supervision of Moscow specialists. And yet an incident occurred. Initially, the bottom plate of the tank was made of welded metal, and when it was filled with water during the test run, the bottom began to bend and then burst open. After that, the reinforced concrete floor was urgently devised. In 1931, when the tower was commissioned, the 700 cubic meter water tank was the largest in the world. It was welded right on the spot, and at night one could see the blue welding lights even from Sverdlovsk. And it turned out to be something special! The tank, through its reinforced concrete ring, rests on four points: two free-standing supports and two brick walls of the staircase. Located at the highest point of the settlement, the tower has become its architectural symbol. Upon completion, the tower was whitelimed, hence the name. The tower changed its color only once, during the World War II, when it was painted in khaki shade for disguise.
Over time, the workers’ settlement grew so large that even the giant tank could no longer maintain the required water pressure. Lake Shuvakish was nearly drained, and the tower became irrelevant. It stopped functioning in the 1960s, and in 1974 it turned into an architectural monument. Uralmash watched over the structure in the Soviet years, but in 1990s the plant itself faced difficulties, and the tower decayed. The city could not afford its maintenance, and there were constant disputes about who should restore the abandoned structure. In 2006, the building was taken over by the Red Cross, but that did not change much.
The local enthusiasts returned the architectural monument in the spotlight for the residents and authorities of Yekaterinburg. In 2012, a group of young architecture students named PODELNIKI was established. Group members initiated works to save and preserve the tower, cleaned it of debris and made it safe to visit, installed electricity and heat guns. Since August 2016, the White Tower has been operating as a museum of itself: visitors can watch a film about the history of the monument on a multimedia screen, take part in guided tours and cultural events, and buy souvenirs. All raised funds are used to finance the further restoration of this symbol of the Constructivist era. This means that the famous White Tower is coming back to life.
Elena Malinovskaya

This unique structure in

stands out for its bold forms: a huge cylindrical tank literally floats in the air, supported by thin reinforced concrete columns and a stairwell. The snow-white color of the tower, which gave it its name, emphasizes the clean lines and geometry characteristic of the Avant-garde era.

What to Do

The main reason to visit the
White Tower
is its incredible architectural aesthetic. You can examine in detail how the cylindrical tank connects to the supports and appreciate the famous
round windows
, which became a hallmark of the Constructivist style. It is an ideal spot for photoshoots, especially in sunny weather when the white concrete contrasts strikingly with the blue sky.
In addition to the exterior inspection, it is worth paying attention to the information boards telling the story of the site's restoration. Occasionally, the venue hosts cultural events, lectures on the avant-garde, and themed tours that allow you to learn how the world's largest tank (at the time of construction) was designed.
A walk by the tower is best combined with exploring
Kultury Boulevard
and the adjacent "socgorod" (socialist city). Walking through the district, you will see how the tower dominates the space, closing the perspective of the streets and remaining the main vertical landmark that preserves the spirit of the heroic industrialization of the 1930s.
Getting There

White Tower
is located in the Ordzhonikidzevsky District at
2 Bakinskikh Komissarov St
. Getting there from the city center is quite easy: by car, the trip takes about 15–20 minutes via Prospekt Kosmonavtov.

Found an inaccuracy?
The history of this structure began in 1928, when construction started on the industrial giant—the Uralmash plant—in
Yekaterinburg
(then Sverdlovsk). The water tower project, designed by the young architect
Moisei Reisher
, was approved as the most progressive: the author prepared the sketch in just one day, proposing a bold use of reinforced concrete.
Construction was completed in 1931, but the launch was not without dramatic events. During the first test, the bottom of the massive metal tank could not withstand the pressure of 750 cubic meters of water and burst. The structure was later reinforced with a reinforced concrete base designed by engineer
Sergey Prokhorov
, and the tower successfully served the city until the 1960s.
During the Soviet era, the site was recognized as an architectural monument of federal significance; however, after being decommissioned, it remained neglected for a long time. A new life for the tower began in 2012 thanks to the initiative of the
"Podelniki"
architectural group, who took on the task of conservation and transforming the historical site into a modern cultural venue.

about 2 hours
for your walk. This will allow you not only to examine the Constructivist details but also to feel the atmosphere of one of the city's most characteristic districts.
Working Hours

As an architectural monument, the
White Tower
is available for exterior viewing
24/7
. You can admire its forms and take photos at any convenient time, as it is located in an open area.
Since the interior of the tower functions as a cultural venue with a variable event schedule, we strongly recommend checking the official website or the project's social media pages before planning a visit that includes going inside.
